page: Google Cloud Platform m4-ultramem-56 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the memory-optimized m4 family. It features 56 dedicated vCPUs and 1488.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of approximately 26.57 GB per core. This instance type does not include integrated GPUs or local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage.

From a resource density perspective, the m4-ultramem-56 represents a specialized hardware class designed for memory-bound workloads rather than general-purpose compute. The absence of local NVMe SSDs and GPUs represents a clear architectural tradeoff, focusing the hardware profile entirely on massive RAM capacity. Cost efficiency is optimized for workloads that require large datasets to reside entirely in memory, reducing the need for disk-based caching systems.

This server configuration is designed for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, real-time data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise applications. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing performance for workloads that cannot tolerate CPU scheduling latency.
